## How Do LLMs Work? Transformers Explained (2026)
Large language models work by predicting the next token in a sequence, trained on trillions of examples of human text. A token is a word or sub-word unit — the word "understanding" might be split into "under" + "stand" + "ing." The model sees a sequence of tokens, computes probability distributions over its entire vocabulary (typically 100,000-200,000 tokens), and selects the most likely continuation. This process repeats, one token at a time, until the response is complete. [...] That last row matters more than it looks. At the very end of the network, only the last vector in the sequence is multiplied by the unembedding matrix to produce the next-token distribution. Every other vector in the final layer is "wasted" at inference time — but during training, every position predicts its own next token in parallel, which is what makes the math tractable on trillion-token corpora. ### Embedd

plan.title: How ChatGPT Works: Predicting One Token at a Time
plan.description: Large language models like ChatGPT work by predicting the next token, again and again. This video explains tokens, the transformer, training and the human feedback that makes a chatbot helpful.

beats.narration: ChatGPT can write essays, code and poems. Yet underneath, it does one thing only: it guesses the next small piece of text. Then it does it again. How can that be enough?

props.title: How does ChatGPT actually work?
props.subtitle: One simple guess, repeated again and again

beats.narration: Think of your phone's autocomplete, but trained on trillions of examples of human writing. It does not look up answers. It predicts what most likely comes next.
The model reads text in pieces called tokens. A token is a word or part of a word. Understanding might split into under, stand and ing.

props.definition: A word or sub-word unit of text. The word "understanding" might be split into "under" + "stand" + "ing."

beats.narration: For every guess, the model scores its whole vocabulary, typically 100,000 to 200,000 tokens. Each gets a probability. Then one is picked, added to the text, and the loop starts over.

props.heading: One guess
items: Score every token in the vocabulary

beats.narration: This is called autoregressive generation. The model has no plan. It does not know how the sentence ends when it starts. Every coherent paragraph emerges one token at a time.

props.text: The model has no plan: every paragraph emerges one token at a time.

beats.narration: The engine inside is called a transformer. Its key trick is attention, which lets every token gather context from all the earlier tokens, passing it through many stacked blocks.
Here is the flow. Words become tokens. Tokens become numbers called embeddings. Attention blocks mix in context. Out come probabilities for the next token.
Training is a giant fill-in-the-blank game. The model sees text, predicts each next token, and a loss function measures how wrong it was. It never gets the answer as input.

steps.label: Show text
steps.detail: Later words are hidden by a mask

beats.narration: Then backpropagation nudges the embeddings, attention layers and other parameters. Repeat across countless batches, and continuations that fit similar contexts become more probable.
This pre-training is the workhorse. Predicting the next word over billions of tokens teaches grammar, word meanings, facts and long-range links. The result is called a base model.
But a base model only continues text. It is not trying to help you. So how does it become a helpful assistant?

props.text: A base model continues text. It does not try to help.

beats.narration: First, people write example answers, and the model is fine-tuned on them. Then labelers rank several model responses, and those rankings train a separate reward model.
Finally, reinforcement learning tunes the language model to earn higher scores from that reward model, so its answers match what people prefer. This is RLHF.

props.definition: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: a reward model that rates responses guides the language model's learning.
props.example: Used to turn a base model into ChatGPT

beats.narration: So remember this. ChatGPT is a next-token predictor, trained on huge text, then shaped by human feedback. Fluent, yes, but built from one guess at a time.

props.text: A next-token predictor, shaped by human feedback.
